# Chapter 5 - sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Societal dependence on digital services - WannaCry stopping hospital
appointments; systemic, cascading risk - NotPetya spreading from one Ukrainian
software vendor to ports and factories worldwide; under-investment as market
failure - Colonial Pipeline, where one company's weakness interrupted fuel
supply for a region. (2) GDPR and DORA are regulations: Directly binding,
applying as-is (in Norway via the EEA, with the Personal Data Act giving the
GDPR effect). NIS2 is a directive: It binds only through national implementing
law, which for Norway additionally requires EEA incorporation first. (3) What is
in force is the Digital Security Act (adopted 2023, in force 1 October 2025),
which implements NIS1 - covering operators of essential services and digital
service providers, supervised by NSM. NIS2 has not yet been incorporated into
the EEA agreement and is therefore not yet Norwegian law; it is the stricter
benchmark to come. (4) Early warning by Wednesday 09:00 (24h); notification by
Friday 09:00 (72h); final report within one month, i.e. by the same date next
month. Needed in advance: The authority contact points and reporting templates,
and a preparedness plan naming who assesses, who drafts and who signs (Lecture
12). (5) Compliance is a floor set for everyone in the same situation, while
security means controls matched to your actual risks - so every box can be
ticked while a real weakness stands open. An ISMS serves both: Run honestly, it
produces security, and its documentation is simultaneously the evidence of
compliance. Chasing the certificate alone produces neither.
